newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-WEEKEND PROGRAMME IN GERMAN FIRST DIVISION.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WEEKEND PROGRAMME IN GERMAN FIRST DIVISION.

text.p: Bottom club Freiburg started the second half of the season last weekend with a 1-0 defeat at Werder Bremen and desperately need points. German Cup semifinalists Hamburg have won just once away this season.

European Cup quarter-finalists Dortmund returned from the winter break with a superb 3-1 defeat of rivals Bayer Leverkusen and should be unchanged. Relegation-threatened Fortuna have only two home two victories.
Both teams need points to escape relegation zone. St Pauli, who lost 3-0 at Bayern Munich last week, should be able to welcome back Stefan Hanke on to right side of midfield after broken arm.

Hansa managed a 1-1 draw at Karlsruhe last weekend but both teams have been disappointing this season. Bremen's German international midfielder Marco Bode expected to be given a role as out-and-out striker again.

One of the most interesting clashes of the weekend with both teams still in the running for a German league and cup double. Stuttgart, the most entertaining team of the first half of the season, need to bounce back after 1-0 defeat at Schalke but will be missing suspended Dutch libero Frank Verlaat. Karlsruhe on a high after midweek German Cup quarter-final victory over Bayern Munich. German international midfielder Thomas Haessler made a remarkable return in the tie after injury and can be expected to play some of the game.

Borussia bounced back from calamitous first half of the season with 2-0 win at Bielefeld last weekend. With former German international midfielder Stefan Effenberg and Swedish striker Martin Dahlin both fit again 'Gladbach's form should improve dramatically in second half.

Promoted Bochum have been one of the biggest surprises this season. Bayern will need to improve dramatically after their midweek cup defeat. The Bavarians should be at full strength. Bochum have not beaten Bayern at home since the 1985-86 season but they have not lost at home this season.

Leverkusen, an outside bet for the championship, should be unchanged from team defeated at Dortmund last weekend. Have never lost at home to Duisburg. Christoph Daum's team must pick up three points from games like this if they want to challenge Bayern and Dortmund for the title.
After disappointing last few seasons improving Cologne opened the second half of the season with a 2-0 defeat of Duesseldorf. Their midfielder Ralf Hauptmann is suspended.
